title: Phase 0 history rewrite
issueTitle: Phase 0 — History rewrite: purge secrets and data from the six bot repositories
function: Phase 0 of the BotTools consolidation purges secrets and legacy data from the histories of the six bot repositories: KotlinBottools, GKB2, GKB, BotTools, TrumpBot and Support. The legacy data is first copied out byte-exactly, with a manifest of the blobs to purge; then each repository is rewritten with `git filter-repo` in a mirror clone, in a fixed order, and must pass its exit tests on a fresh mirror. KotlinBottools gains a root-anchored `.gitignore` and a gitleaks CI job and becomes public with secret scanning and push protection; what GitHub still serves of the old histories is measured and reported. The phase moves no version.

impact.summary: No module is published and no version moves. Every commit id changes in all six repositories: GKB2, GKB, BotTools, TrumpBot and Support are force-pushed in place, and KotlinBottools becomes public as a fresh repository with every number reproduced, the pre-rewrite repository kept private and archived as `KotlinBottools-legacy`. On `main`, the path scrub replaces the machine-local paths in two KotlinBottools source files, and the rest is repository infrastructure.

release.note: a tracking plan moves no version, and no unit publishes a module

downstream.summary: Every commit id changes, as each root commit holds a purged path; ten commits are pruned and every branch survives. Pre-rewrite ids already cited stay as dated citations that resolve only in the private legacy repository. KotlinBottools has been public since 2026-11-08, so its pre-rewrite objects stay anonymously readable until the swap, a window the residual report states.

Every file and commit message that names a machine-local path is rewritten: the project-checkouts folder becomes `%PROJECTS%` and a user-profile folder `%USERPROFILE%`. On `main` that changes the local Maven repository line of `build.gradle.kts`, which resolved only on this machine, and a commented-out line of `GuildDataParser.kt`; the legacy repository keeps the original text, and the other five repositories are not scrubbed.

The public `KotlinBottools` is a new repository with a new id and the old settings and access; stars and watchers start empty. Until the swap the pre-rewrite repository stays public under its current name; the swap makes it private between its rename and its archiving, and `KotlinBottools-legacy` keeps the pre-rewrite history, its pull requests, milestone and labels, private and archived.

Every number is reproduced, pull requests by closed placeholders, and dropped relationships are re-created, so citations keep resolving. A transfer rewrites the references in the moved text to full names: after the walk they name `KotlinBottools-next` for the issues that moved, which keep resolving through the rename's redirect while no repository takes that name. The 56 links that name the planning branch stop resolving when it is deleted and are pointed at `main`.

KotlinBottools' one allowlist table, scoped to one default rule, one of its own research documents and one exact text, is not part of that alignment, and there is still no global allowlist. Its own CI, Phase 13's, can adopt the same workflow pattern.

items.title: Phase 0 — History rewrite: purge secrets and data from the six bot repositories
Phase 1 — Build skeleton: multi-module build, conventions, CI and repository scaffolding
Phase 2 — Core foundation: ids, failures, settings, storage ports and configuration
Phase 3 — Command model: definitions, validation, typed invocation, dispatch and help
Phase 4 — SQLite storage: migrations, erasure and backups
Phase 5 — Bot runtime: plugins, events, gateway, jobs, registration and built-in commands
Phase 6a — HTTP call surface: the bottools-http API, endpoint vocabulary, failures and test fake
Phase 6b — WebTools adapter: the internal adapter, composite build, strict pin, alignment checks and CI lanes
Phase 7 — Stats provider framework: provider SPI, account links, match tracker and game news
Phase 8 — Reaction-roles plugin, with the default role and welcome message on join
Phase 10 — Admin plugin: typed get and set over guild settings
Phase 11 — Weather plugin: conditions and forecast from Open-Meteo
Phase 12 — Feeds plugin: RSS and Atom subscriptions with content safeguards
Phase 17 — Release 1.0.0 to Maven Central and archive the predecessor repositories
Phase 18 — Published test fixtures for plugin and provider authors (Experimental)
Phase 19 — Poker plugin: playable Texas hold 'em (Experimental)
